theorem_title: The refined child is positive and strictly smaller
natural_language_statement:
For natural parameters $L,\varepsilon,z$, put $A=4z+2\varepsilon+1$, $P=2^LA-1$, and $Q=3\cdot2^{L-2}A-1$. When $L<2$, the exponent $L-2$ uses truncated natural subtraction.

Assume $L\ge2$; no parity restriction on $\varepsilon$ is needed. Then

$$
0<P,\quad0<Q<P,\quad Q=\left\lfloor\frac{3P-1}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

This proves the size comparison used by the later guarded coalescence result.
formal_statement:
theorem CollatzWork.refinedChild_arithmetic (L epsilon z : Nat) (hL : 2 ≤ L) :
    0 < refinedParent L epsilon z ∧
    0 < refinedChild L epsilon z ∧
    refinedChild L epsilon z < refinedParent L epsilon z ∧
    refinedChild L epsilon z = (3 * refinedParent L epsilon z - 1) / 4 := by sorry
